title: Flu Cases High as Early Outbreak Spreads in Japan
paragraphs: As the weather gets colder in Japan, flu cases usually rise. But this year, the virus has been spreading across the country earlier than usual.

Japan's health ministry watches flu cases at about 3,000 medical institutions across the country. It considers the flu to be at "outbreak" level when each of those institutions reports an average of one flu patient in a week.

All of Japan's 47 prefectures were already above this level at the end of August — making the start of this year's flu season about a month earlier than last year's, and the second-earliest start since records began being kept in 1999.
And according to government figures, by the week of September 21 to September 27, there were an average of 7.2 flu patients per medical institution.
This was a little lower than the previous week, however, when the average was 8.5.
That may sound like good news. But a health ministry official said the decrease may only be temporary, as in previous years, flu cases have fallen before rising again.
And the situation isn't the same across the country.
In Japan, when flu cases hit an average of 10 patients per medical institution per week, that's considered a "caution" level outbreak. At 30 patients, it's considered "warning" level.
By the last full week of September, Okinawa was well above the "warning" level, with medical institutions there reporting an average of 42.5 patients that week — the highest figure in Japan.
Meanwhile, Saitama, Ibaraki, Aichi and Gifu were all above the 10-patient level. Of these four prefectures, Saitama had the highest figure, with more than 14 patients per medical institution.
The health ministry is asking people across Japan to take basic steps to help stop the flu from spreading. People should wash their hands regularly, and cover their mouths when they cough.
